narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Product Shelf"**

The site is a frame, not a brand. A cool concrete ground with graphite ink holds the page and owns no hue of its own; colour arrives only with the work. Each shipped product gets a full-bleed band painted in that app's own palette (Liftrix graphite and orange, Linaw forest and leaf, tortui slate and cyan), and the fixed masthead takes on the world of whichever band is passing beneath it. Leaving a product band returns you to concrete.

Density is editorial and sparse: one large condensed grotesque headline per region, generous band padding, and information organised by hairline rules rather than boxes. The only objects with physical presence are the products themselves, shown as running loops inside realistic CSS phones and a terminal window, and the hero shows two of them side by side, never overlapping. Everything else is flat type on a ground.

Three faces divide the work cleanly. Bricolage Grotesque, condensed and tightly tracked, carries every headline; Schibsted Grotesk carries reading text and controls; Martian Mono is reserved for data (platforms, versions, stacks) and for tortui's own name, which ends in a blinking cyan caret.
keyCharacteristics: A colourless concrete frame; every hue on the page belongs to a product.
Full-bleed project bands, each a complete world of six tokens (ground, ink, muted, line, accent, on-accent).
A fixed masthead that inherits the band beneath it and condenses the full name to "KA" on scroll.
Sticky project summary beside a scrolling media and notes column on wide screens.
Hairline rules for structure; drop shadows only on device objects.
Every looping video carries a visible, keyboard-reachable play/pause control.

rules.name: The No House Colour Rule
rules.body: The frame's accent is its own ink. A new frame surface gets graphite on concrete; any hue it shows must come from a product's world, inside that product's band or media.

rules.name: The Six-Token World Rule
rules.body: A world is exactly `--bg`, `--ink`, `--muted`, `--line`, `--accent` and `--on-accent`, declared on a `[data-theme]` selector. Components read only these custom properties, so a component works in every world without variants. Adding a product means adding one theme block, never per-component colour overrides.

rules.name: The Terminal Is Always Tortui Rule
rules.body: The terminal window keeps tortui's slate, ink and cyan wherever it appears, because it is tortui's own product chrome.

rules.name: The Condensed Headline Rule
rules.body: Every Bricolage heading uses a reduced width axis (wdth 85 to 90) and negative tracking (-0.02em to -0.035em); larger sizes track tighter. Body sizes never use Bricolage.

rules.name: The Mono Means Data Rule
rules.body: Martian Mono sets only machine-shaped content: platforms, versions, tech stacks, commands and a terminal product's name. It never sets prose, headings for non-terminal products, or labels above headings.

rules.name: The Only Objects Cast Shadows Rule
rules.body: A blur shadow means "this is a device you could hold". Buttons, rows, masthead and sections never get one.

dos: **Do** add a new product as one `[data-theme]` block of six custom properties and a full-bleed band; let every component read the variables.
**Do** keep concrete (#e7e7e3) and graphite (#121316) as the only colours of frame regions.
**Do** set headings in Bricolage at a reduced width axis with negative tracking, and reading text in Schibsted Grotesk.
**Do** separate content with 1px hairlines at the world's line colour; open lists with a full-ink rule.
**Do** show products as real captures inside CSS device frames, and give every loop a visible 44px play/pause control placed off the app UI.
**Do** route world colour changes through the 650ms ease-out transition (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`) and make them instant under reduced motion.
**Do** keep every tap target at least 44px tall.
donts: **Don't** give the frame an accent hue; graphite is its accent.
**Don't** put blur shadows on chrome (buttons, masthead, rows, sections); shadows belong to devices and icons.
**Don't** set prose, non-terminal product names or labels above headings in Martian Mono.
**Don't** wrap projects in same-size cards on a shared ground; each product owns a full-bleed band.
**Don't** hard-code a world colour inside a component that can appear in more than one world; only the terminal (always tortui) and the phone (device materials) carry literal colours.
